span.label: AND THE AUTHORS LATER USE THAT ARBITRARINESS AGAINST THEIR OWN RESULT: `Quotation withheld`. A DEFINITIONAL CHOICE DECLARED ARBITRARY WHEN IT IS MADE AND THEN CITED AS A REASON TO DISCOUNT A FINDING THIRTY-FIVE THOUSAND CHARACTERS LATER. The same paper does it a third time near the end - `the computation of local rates of reinforcement is MOST ARBITRARY AT EARLY AND LATE TIMES after reinforcement` - so the qualification is tracked, not mentioned once and forgotten.

span.label: temporal separation → time since reinforcement
span.note: THE TWO CANNOT BE SEPARATED IN THIS STUDY - the DESIGN form (Q-286/Q-287). It bounds what the paper's own results can mean, and it lives in a methods paragraph where nothing downstream will find it. A 1968 methods sentence naming its own confound, in a paper nobody would search for it in.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `local rate of reinforcement` - AN OPERATIONAL DEFINITION ITS OWN AUTHORS CALL ARBITRARY, WITH THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVES NAMED: other assignments of time to opportunities are `possible, SUCH AS BISECTION ... USING THE GEOMETRIC RATHER THAN THE ARITHMETIC MEAN, or the assignment to a given opportunity of the time since the last opportunity. THE PRESENT TECHNIQUE, THOUGH ARBITRARY, SEEMS TO INVOLVE THE SIMPLEST AD HOC ASSUMPTIONS.` The choice is defended on SIMPLICITY, not on correctness, and the competitors are printed so a reader can substitute one. This record's `senses[0]` and `senses[1]` already distinguish the overall from the local rate; **this is the further fact that the local one is a construct with a dial on it.**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `Reinforcements per opportunity` - A NAME SHAPED LIKE A RATE THAT DENOTES A PROBABILITY. `Quotation withheld` The `X per Y` form is how this literature writes rates (`reinforcements per hour` appears in the same paper), so the name invites the reader to expect a count over a denominator and delivers a bounded probability instead. **The definition is explicit precisely because the name is misleading.**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `opportunity for reinforcement` - THE DEFINITION IS A DISJUNCTION, AND THE TWO LIMBS ARE NOT THE SAME TEST. `a point on the continuum of time since reinforcement AT WHICH THE PROBABILITY OF REINFORCEMENT IS GREATER THAN ZERO, OR AT WHICH AT LEAST ONE INTERVAL ENDS.` The first limb is a property of the schedule; the second is a property of the sample of intervals actually run. They coincide in the limit and can differ in a finite experiment.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: qualifies → Reynolds and Catania (1961); Catania and Reynolds (1963) — the authors' own earlier publication
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE FUNCTION IS FITTED TO A GROUP OR TO AN ANIMAL, AND WHY THE FORM WAS CHOSEN. Two admissions in one passage: 'THE CHOICE BETWEEN THESE TWO FUNCTIONS WAS BASED MORE ON LOGICAL CONSIDERATIONS ... THAN ON THE SUPERIORITY OF THE FIT of the power function to the data', and 'Quotation withheld' The published law was fitted to the group average, chosen on a priori grounds rather than fit, and fails on every individual - said by its own authors
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: qualifies → Reynolds and Catania (1962); Reynolds (1966); Stubbs (1968)
span.note: differs in: CAPACITY VERSUS CONTROL. 'the performances maintained by FI schedules DO NOT APPEAR TO BE AS WELL UNDER THE CONTROL OF TIME SINCE REINFORCEMENT Quotation withheld.' What an animal CAN discriminate and what its behaviour IS controlled by come apart, so a discrimination result does not license an inference about what governs performance
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: builds-on → Millenson (1966); Anger (1956)
span.note: differs in: WHAT AN UNEXPECTED DIRECTION OF CHANGE IS TAKEN TO SHOW. Inter-response times shorten 'EVEN IN SCHEDULES OF REINFORCEMENT IN WHICH LONG IRTs ARE DIFFERENTIALLY REINFORCED', i.e. against the contingency, and the literature's reading is a property of the reinforcement process itself - 'that Quotation withheld'. A behaviour that moves opposite to the arranged contingency is explained by postulating an asymmetry in what reinforcement can act on
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · local rate of reinforcement —distinct-from→ overall rate of reinforcement
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span stated a conclusion without naming either rate. This sentence names both AND DISTINGUISHES THEM BY EXPERIMENT: 'If the distribution of intervals in a schedule is changed WHILE THE OVERALL RATE OF REINFORCEMENT IS HELD CONSTANT, the decrease in the LOCAL RATE OF REINFORCEMENT...' - one is held fixed while the other moves, which is the strongest form a distinction can take: not observed, but constructed. — strength of the relation: 1
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: terminal rate of responding —part-of→ rate of responding
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The terminal rate is the local rate AT A PARTICULAR MOMENT - a restriction of the general measure, which is why `part-of` and not `is-a`.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: overall rate of reinforcement —causes→ terminal rate of responding
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — DIRECTION CHECKED AGAINST THE SENTENCE, AND MY FIRST VERSION HAD IT BACKWARDS. `the terminal rate of responding ... INCREASED AS the overall rate of reinforcement INCREASED` - the reinforcement rate is what the SCHEDULE SETS and the responding is what the animal does, so the schedule variable is the cause. I wrote the edge the other way round while writing a note that said the reinforcement rate was the manipulated side; the dry run is where that was caught. Weight 0.7 records the paper's own hedge - `In general, however` - stated immediately after `No systematic relationship is evident` for the FI rates.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across seven variable-interval schedules the overall rate of pigeons' key-pecking rose monotonically with the overall rate of reinforcement but with diminishing returns, over a span from 8.4 to 300 reinforcements per hour.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within a single schedule, how fast the bird pecked at a given moment after reinforcement tracked the local rate of reinforcement at that moment, computed from the probability of reinforcement there and the nearness of reinforcement opportunities at other moments.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's overall conclusion is that a schedule's overall response rate is not set by its overall reinforcement rate but is the sum of separate local reinforcement effects distributed across times within the interval.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A schedule engineered to hold the probability of reinforcement constant across time since reinforcement flattened the within-interval response gradient, keeping the local pecking rate roughly constant instead of rising.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Adding extra short intervals raised the probability of reinforcement at t sec and correspondingly raised the local pecking rate exactly at t sec, and adding four such intervals raised it more than adding two.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Including a 0-sec interval (first peck after reinforcement is reinforced) raised responding only in the first two or three time bins after reinforcement, not across the whole interval.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Removing reinforcement at the end of the long interval (replacing it with timeout) destroyed the temporal pattern of responding when the early probability was only 0.05, showing that responding early in an interval is partly sustained by the later, high-probability reinforcement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: At matched overall reinforcement rates, arithmetic variable-interval schedules sustained higher overall response rates than fixed-interval schedules for all but one pigeon.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Reinforcing a response immediately after a preceding reinforcement influenced later responding only briefly, so schedules with and without a 0-sec interval remain comparable at later times.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
